entries.title: Titus 3:1
segments: In subjection to rulers. Through a misapprehension as to the kind of freedom conferred by the gospel, some of the Jews became unruly and disposed to rebellion against the Roman authorities.

entries.title: Titus 3:5
segments: Washing of regeneration. A reference to the symbolism of baptism, which is a setting apart unto regeneration, a step preparatory to the 'renewing of the Holy Spirit.' See

entries.title: Titus 3:9
segments: The law. The Jewish ceremonial law.  The Jew had been trained for centuries to the observance of this law and clung to its ceremonies. Much fruitless argument arose in the effort to preserve the law intact and graft Christianity upon it.

entries.title: Titus 3:11
segments: Perverted. The persistence in error after two admonishing showed that it sprang from inward moral darkness.  The man was 'self condemned' by his love for the cord; for the true spirit of the church was unity.  See

entries.title: Titus 3:12
segments: Nicopolis. The city of that name in Epirus, founded by Augustus in memory of the victory of Actium.

entries.title: Titus 3:13
segments: .  It is supposed that Zenas and Apollos were the bearers of this epistle to Titus.
